name: The Baranoff Oak

location.address: Baranoff Park, downtown Safety Harbor, FL

official_register.name: Live Oak Society (registry number 4760 per a search summary, not confirmed on a fetched page)

access: Free. City-owned pocket park in the middle of downtown Safety Harbor, walk-up; voters were asked in March 2024 to protect the park and tree in perpetuity (WUSF).
transport: NOT reachable from Tampa within 30 minutes by public transport. Safety Harbor is in Pinellas County about 20 miles west of downtown Tampa, roughly 30 minutes by car; PSTA buses reach it only with a change. Label as a day trip by car, and as Safety Harbor, not Tampa.

Moved out of Tampa into its own place, Safety Harbor (not within 30 minutes of Tampa by public transport).
story:
In March 2024 the voters of Safety Harbor were asked to protect one tree in perpetuity. The question covered the Baranoff Oak and the small park around it, in the middle of downtown, and it says a lot about how a town of this size feels about a live oak said to be between 300 and 500 years old.

That range comes from WUSF, Tampa Bay's public radio station, and from a visitors' waymark, and both give it as an estimate. Nobody has counted rings. WUSF adds that it is thought to be the oldest tree in Pinellas County. Take that at the strength it is offered, as a belief rather than a record. The waymark gives the trunk as nearly 20 feet around, about six metres.

For most of its life it was simply the Safety Harbor Oak. It took its present name in 2004, when it became the centrepiece of a new pocket park. Being the centrepiece has not always been kind to it. The Tampa Bay Times once reported that an effort to show the tree off had harmed it, and that arborists worked to restore it. Photographs taken in October 2026 show it alive, its branches spreading wide over the park.

Baranoff Park is free and open, a walk-up spot in the centre of town. Safety Harbor is its own place, about 20 miles west of downtown Tampa and roughly half an hour by car. Buses reach it, but only with a change.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the wide-spreading live oak the park is built around, its trunk nearly 20 feet, about six metres, round. It stands at the centre of Baranoff Park in downtown Safety Harbor.
